title: Trump Administration Loses Two Court Battles Over Immigration Rules
summary:
Imagine you're an exchange student in a new country, and suddenly you're told you have to leave after four years — even if you're in the middle of a degree. That's what almost happened to about 1.6 million international students in the U.S.

On Monday, a federal judge blocked the Trump administration from imposing fixed time limits on how long foreign students and journalists can remain in the country without applying for extensions. Under the proposed rule, F visas for international students and J visas for exchange programs would be capped at four years. I visas for journalists would be limited to 240 days.

Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV, who was appointed by Republican President George W. Bush, called the government's reasoning "exceptionally weak." He warned that the damage to higher education and the wider U.S. economy would be "catastrophic."

At the same time, a coalition of 22 states and the District of Columbia — led by New York, California and Illinois — filed lawsuits to stop a separate rule. That rule would allow immigration officers to deny green cards to immigrants who use public benefits like food assistance or Medicaid. The lawsuits argue the administration overstepped its authority by bypassing Congress.

A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson defended the regulation, calling the plaintiffs "left-wing leaders" who were "terrified they will lose federal funds." New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the rule "seeks to push immigrant families away from the programs that have kept people fed and healthy for decades."
why_it_matters: Your classmates, your future college and the doctors and nurses in your community can all be affected by immigration rules — this story shows how courts and states can push back when they think the government has gone too far.

background_read: A visa is a permission slip from a country that lets someone from another country come to study, work or visit for a set time.
The Department of Homeland Security (the U.S. government department in charge of immigration and protecting the country) made the rules that are being challenged.
Medicaid is a government health program that helps people with low incomes pay for doctor visits and medicine.

WHAT: A judge blocked fixed time limits on student and journalist visas, while at the same time states sued over a separate rule that would let officers deny green cards to immigrants who use public benefits.
WHERE: In U.S. federal courts — the visa case before Judge Saylor, and the green card lawsuits filed by 22 states and Washington, D.C.
WHY: About 1.6 million international students could be affected, and the judge warned the harm to higher education and the U.S. economy would be 'catastrophic.'
